input.summary:
P1 kitchen furnished in parts/room-12.mjs: stove run on the hearth wall (furnace, lit smoker, barrel), table in the NE corner (oak fence + pressure plate) with two stair chairs, hanging lantern, potted poppy. In a scratch copy it reads OK: walk 9/9, light min 11, no dark cell, fit OK.
The real build.nbt places 0 of its blocks: runParts refuses all 9 writes because the shell's interior air is locked (see left).
Scratch check file: room12-test.nbt (not build.nbt); room.png shows the kitchen from above.
left: BLOCKER (pipeline, not this module): runParts locks every cell an earlier part set, air included (build.mjs write(): owned.has(k) -> refused). The shell (shell-west/shell-east house() carves interior air) owns all room interiors, so every room part's writes are refused: P1 kitchen REFUSED 9 of 9 (27,2,18 oak_stairs vs air; 28,2,18 oak_fence vs air; etc.). The spec says 'build only into air', which the lock contradicts. Fix needed upstream: let later parts write into air the shell left (lock only solid cells), or have room parts run without the air lock. Until then the real build has no kitchen furniture.

Design to re-check once unlocked: layout in parts/room-12.mjs (layers at origin [26,2,18]: y2 furnace (26,2,20), smoker lit (27,2,20), barrel (28,2,20), oak fence (28,2,18) with oak_stairs chairs at (27,2,18) facing west and (28,2,19) facing south; y3 pressure plate (28,3,18), potted poppy (28,3,20); y4 hanging lantern (27,4,19)). Lanes (26,2..3,18..19) kept clear for the west doorway at x25 z18..19.

Spec mismatch: the brief puts the kitchen door at (26,2..3,19) inside the room box, but the plan's walls put the hall doorway on x25 (z18..19). I kept x26 z18..19 clear as the lane for x25, and placed nothing at the door cells. The plan grid also shows 'D' on z17 x25..28 and x29 z18..19; those are unbuilt-wall artifacts (the spec says z17 is solid partition; x29 holds windows). Not verified against a built shell.
plan.md Notes and elements.md not ticked: part 19 is not one of the six checklist parts, and the kitchen has no element line of its own.

waste.what: Floor-grid parsing and furniture placement by hand: I worked out each cell's facing and state (stairs facing back-to-wall, furnace/smoker facing north, barrel top) for a 3x3 room.
waste.cost: about 3 layer attempts, one row fix, roughly 25 blocks
waste.tool: A room-level designer command that takes a furniture spec (table, chairs, stove run, light) and emits the layers() rows and legend, plus facing rules for stairs and furnaces.

waste.what: Diagnosing the lock: finding that the shell's air interior blocks every room write needed reading build.mjs's write() and owned-set logic.
waste.cost: 3 tool calls and a source read of runParts
waste.tool: runParts should report the owner of a refused cell (which earlier part set it, and whether it was air) in one line, and a room-only dry run that applies a part to a copy of build.nbt without the lock. That would have shown the blocker in one pass.

waste.what: Workaround test: I applied the part to a scratch copy with plain load()+build()+save() to check walk, light and fit, bypassing runParts. That is not the real pipeline result and is only a design check.
waste.cost: one scratch script, one room/fit/check/rooms run
waste.tool: mcd room with a --part flag that runs one part's build against build.nbt and reports refused cells, so the check uses the real lock and no scratch path.
